challenges.name: confident-wrong-answer-evidence
challenges.title: The Confident Wrong Answer: read the evidence
challenges.description: The CodeDev support bot told a learner to call submitLesson({ lessonId, force: true }), an option that never existed. Six statements on one evidence pack - the chat transcript (A), the prompt that was sent (B), the current docs (C) and the request log (D) - take you from reading the evidence to a hypothesis, past a wrong explanation, to the fix and its verification.

questions.question:
Evidence A - support widget, conversation sb_77f3:
21:14:02  learner u_5521  How do I submit my lesson when one hidden test still fails?
21:14:07  support bot     You can force the submission. Call submitLesson({ lessonId, force: true }) from your lab script: the force flag skips the hidden tests and marks the lesson as submitted. It has been supported since @codedev/lab 1.4.
21:31:40  learner u_5521  I tried it: CodeDevLabError: submitLesson: unknown option "force" (expected { lessonId, attemptId }). What now?

Evidence C - https://app.codedev.test/docs/lab/submit:
submitLesson({ lessonId, attemptId })                      @codedev/lab 2.x
  lessonId   string   the lesson to submit
  attemptId  string   the attempt created by `codedev test`
An attempt with a failing test is rejected (status "rejected", failedTests listed).
Tests cannot be skipped: fix the test, run `codedev test` again and submit the new attemptId.
CHANGELOG
2.0.0  2025-09-15  submitLesson(lessonId) is replaced by submitLesson({ lessonId, attemptId })
1.4.0  2024-11-02  codedev test prints the attempt id
1.0.0  2024-03-11  first release: submitLesson(lessonId)

Statement: "The force option does not exist in any version of @codedev/lab, so the bot did not repeat outdated documentation: it produced an option that was never documented."
questions.explanation: True. The changelog in C lists every signature: 1.0 had submitLesson(lessonId), 2.0 has submitLesson({ lessonId, attemptId }), and 1.4 only changed what codedev test prints. No version has force, so this is not an outdated fact from before the model's cutoff (that would have been the 1.x call submitLesson(lessonId)): it is a hallucination. Telling the two apart matters, because outdated knowledge points at the cutoff while an invented option shows the model filling a gap. The common mistake is to call every wrong answer "outdated training data".

questions.question:
Evidence A - support widget, conversation sb_77f3:
21:14:02  learner u_5521  How do I submit my lesson when one hidden test still fails?
21:14:07  support bot     You can force the submission. Call submitLesson({ lessonId, force: true }) from your lab script: the force flag skips the hidden tests and marks the lesson as submitted. It has been supported since @codedev/lab 1.4.
21:31:40  learner u_5521  I tried it: CodeDevLabError: submitLesson: unknown option "force" (expected { lessonId, attemptId }). What now?

Statement: "Because the answer names an exact call, explains what the flag does and gives the version it appeared in, it was probably checked against the documentation and is more likely to be correct than a vaguer answer."
questions.explanation: False. A model produces detail the same way it produces everything else: as likely next tokens. The precise call, the explanation and "since @codedev/lab 1.4" are all invented (C shows 1.4 changed something else). Nothing in the bot looked anything up: the prompt in B carried no documentation. The misconception is that confidence and detail signal verification; only a source the claim came from, such as a cited docs page, does.

questions.question:
Evidence B - prompt log, request sb_77f3 (the full prompt):
You are the CodeDev support assistant. Be friendly and answer the learner's question.

Question: How do I submit my lesson when one hidden test still fails?

Evidence C - https://app.codedev.test/docs/lab/submit:
submitLesson({ lessonId, attemptId })                      @codedev/lab 2.x
  lessonId   string   the lesson to submit
  attemptId  string   the attempt created by `codedev test`
An attempt with a failing test is rejected (status "rejected", failedTests listed).
Tests cannot be skipped: fix the test, run `codedev test` again and submit the new attemptId.
CHANGELOG
2.0.0  2025-09-15  submitLesson(lessonId) is replaced by submitLesson({ lessonId, attemptId })
1.4.0  2024-11-02  codedev test prints the attempt id
1.0.0  2024-03-11  first release: submitLesson(lessonId)

Evidence D - support-bot request log:
2026-10-20T21:14:07.418Z support-bot req=sb_77f3 user=u_5521 model=chat-small-2025-01 knowledge_cutoff=2025-01 temperature=0.2 input_tokens=41 output_tokens=58 docs_attached=0 finish_reason=stop latency_ms=1840

Statement: "The model's training data ends before @codedev/lab 2.0 was released, the prompt carried no documentation, and nothing in it allowed an "I'm not sure" - together that left the model to fill the gap with a plausible guess."
questions.explanation: True. D gives knowledge_cutoff=2025-01 and C dates the 2.0 change to 2025-09-15, so the model cannot have learned the current call. D also shows docs_attached=0 and B confirms the prompt holds only a persona and the question. "Be friendly and answer the learner's question" asks for an answer every time, with no way out. Knowledge cutoff, missing context and a vague prompt together explain the confident invented answer. The common mistake is to stop at one cause - usually "the model is bad" - when each of the three gaps needs its own fix.

questions.question:
Evidence D - support-bot request log:
2026-10-20T21:14:07.418Z support-bot req=sb_77f3 user=u_5521 model=chat-small-2025-01 knowledge_cutoff=2025-01 temperature=0.2 input_tokens=41 output_tokens=58 docs_attached=0 finish_reason=stop latency_ms=1840

Statement: "The temperature is the cause: with temperature 0 the model would have given the correct 2.x call instead of inventing an option."
questions.explanation: False. Temperature controls how often the model picks a less likely token; 0.2 is already low. At temperature 0 it always picks the most likely token, but without the docs in the prompt the most likely answer is still a guess, so you would get the same wrong answer every time. Lowering the temperature makes an answer repeatable, not true. The misconception is that hallucinations are random noise that sampling settings can turn off; here the missing facts are the cause.

CHANGELOG
2.0.0  2025-09-15  submitLesson(lessonId) is replaced by submitLesson({ lessonId, attemptId })
1.4.0  2024-11-02  codedev test prints the attempt id
1.0.0  2024-03-11  first release: submitLesson(lessonId)

Statement: "A prompt that contains the docs page from C with an id such as [lab-submit-v2], tells the model to answer only from that documentation and cite the id, and allows "I'm not sure" when the docs do not answer, closes the gaps that produced force: true."
questions.explanation: True. Each part closes one gap. The docs page brings the current signature into the context window, so the knowledge cutoff no longer matters for this question. "Answer only from the documentation and cite the id" makes the answer checkable: the widget can link the citation and a test can verify it. The allowed "I'm not sure" gives the model a correct reply when retrieval finds nothing, instead of pressure to invent one. The common shortcut - adding "do not hallucinate" without the docs - adds no facts at all.

questions.question:
Evidence A - support widget, conversation sb_77f3:
21:14:02  learner u_5521  How do I submit my lesson when one hidden test still fails?
21:14:07  support bot     You can force the submission. Call submitLesson({ lessonId, force: true }) from your lab script: the force flag skips the hidden tests and marks the lesson as submitted. It has been supported since @codedev/lab 1.4.
21:31:40  learner u_5521  I tried it: CodeDevLabError: submitLesson: unknown option "force" (expected { lessonId, attemptId }). What now?

Verification note in the fix's pull request:
"Tested on staging: asked 'How do I submit my lesson when one hidden test still fails?' once, got the 2.x call with [lab-submit-v2]. Closing ticket #2291."

Statement: "This check is enough to show that the incident is fixed and will not come back."
questions.explanation: False. One question, asked once, checks one path. It does not check a question the docs do not cover (the bot must say "I'm not sure" there, not invent), it says nothing about the next run if the temperature is above 0, and it will not run again when someone changes the prompt builder. Verification is a small eval set of real questions - each with the source it must cite or the expectation "I'm not sure" - run on recorded fixtures in CI and on the live model before each release. The misconception is to treat one good answer as proof.

challenges.name: confident-wrong-answer-prompt-builder
challenges.title: The Confident Wrong Answer
challenges.description: The CodeDev support bot told a learner to call submitLesson({ lessonId, force: true }) - an option that never existed in @codedev/lab - and the request log shows docs_attached=0. The retrieval step finds the right documentation pages and passes them to buildPrompt(question, docs, options), most relevant first, but the bot still answers from what the model learned before its knowledge cutoff (January 2025) and never says it is unsure. Fix buildPrompt so that the prompt contains the first options.maxDocs documents in the given order (none when maxDocs is 0 or less), each as a line "[<id>] <title>" followed by a line with its text; tells the model to answer only from that documentation and to cite the [id] it used; tells it to reply "I'm not sure" when the documentation does not answer the question; and still contains the question. No real LLM is called: the file contains a fake model that replays recorded answers (do not change it or the test runner). Input: { docs: { id, title, text }[], options: { maxDocs }, questions: string[] }. Output: for each question a line "Q: <question>" and a line "A: <the fake model's answer>".
hints: The fake model can only answer from a page that is in the prompt, and only when the prompt tells it to stay inside the documentation. Print the prompt your buildPrompt returns: which of the docs it received does it actually contain?

Read the fake model's three checks at the top of the "do not change" section: the instruction it looks for, how it recognises a page in the prompt, and what lets it reply "I'm not sure". Then check how many documents you send and what Array.prototype.slice does with a negative end.

A similar prompt for a different bot: "You are the Beanbox order assistant. Use only the menu below and name the [item id] you used. If the menu does not list it, say: not on the menu." followed by "[latte-m] Latte, medium" and its price line, then "Order: one medium latte". The rule, the way out and the sources are three separate parts of the prompt.
